decisionsTitle: The team's undertaking at every sign-in: owed once per sign-in, the session carrying the moment it was signed in, every acceptance kept with the sign-in it answers (amends §1006)
decisionsSection:
**The brief, 2026-11-20 (amending §1006):** the team's undertaking is owed at every sign-in, not once per account — the same people as §1006, every colleague below the Administrator, the version in force accepted once per sign-in session —, and every acceptance is kept, so the club can show that the person accepted it at each sign-in. §1006 had asked it once per account and version.

**What was there.** The gate of §1006 in `requireStaff`: a colleague below the Administrator who had not accepted the version in force — once, ever — was sent to `/admin/acord`; the acceptance was one row per account and version (`staff_team_agreement_acceptances`, `UNIQUE (staff_user_id, legal_document_id)`). Auth.js's token carried the account's id alone, and so did the development switcher's cookie.

**Decision.**

- **The session carries the moment it was signed in.** Auth.js's `jwt` callback (`src/auth.ts`, over `staffTokenAt` in `staff-identity/auth-callbacks.ts`) writes `signedInAt` — milliseconds since the epoch — when Zitadel hands it `account`, which happens at a sign-in and at no other call, and returns the token as it came at every other call: a refresh keeps the moment, and an update a browser posts to `/api/auth/session` neither writes nor moves it. The `session` callback hands it to the server (`src/types/next-auth.d.ts`). The development sign-in — the one `yarn dev` and the end-to-end suite use — writes the same moment beside the account's id (`br_dev_staff_at`, `DEV_STAFF_SIGNED_IN_COOKIE`), and «Ieși din cont» drops both. `session.ts` reads the session once per render (`sessionThisRequest`, React's `cache`): the account and its moment.
- **Owed unless accepted at or after this sign-in, or for it** (`teamAgreementOwedThisSession`, pure, in `staff-identity/domain/team-agreement.ts`): never the Administrators, nobody while no version is in force; a session that carries its moment owes the version in force unless the account accepted it at or after that moment — the acceptance of the sign-in before does not answer, an acceptance made since on another device does — or an acceptance names this very sign-in. The last clause is for the clocks: the press's moment is read by the server that took the press, the sign-in's by the one that took the sign-in, and a press on a server whose clock ran behind would be stored a little before the sign-in it answers; compared by the moments alone, the gate would ask again and every next press would meet the unique key and write nothing, until sign-out. `outstandingTeamAgreement` reads, in one query, the version in force and two facts folded from the account's acceptances of it — the newest moment, and whether one names this sign-in; a request asks it once however many doors ask (`outstandingThisRequest`, keyed now by the account's id, its role and the moment in milliseconds).
- **A session signed in before this change** carries no moment. It owes the version in force unless the account accepted it in the per-sign-in record at all — every row of which was written since this release —, so it is asked once and not again until its next sign-in, which writes the moment: no token is rewritten, nobody is signed out, nothing loops. The acceptances made once per account under §1006 answer no sign-in.
- **Every acceptance kept**: `staff_team_agreement_sign_in_acceptances`, migration `0225_staff_team_agreement_every_sign_in` (expand only, generated by drizzle-kit: a new table; §1006's table, its key and its rows untouched) — who, the version (`RESTRICT`) with its number and hash, the language, the name typed, the SHA-256 of the text read, the IP address and the browser (§556, §771), the moment, and **the sign-in it answers** (`signed_in_at`; null for a session from before this change); `UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT (staff_user_id, legal_document_id, signed_in_at)`, so a double tap writes nothing, the next sign-in is a row of its own and the sessions from before count as one; `CASCADE` with the account. Audited `staff.team_agreement_accepted` with the version and the sign-in, never the name. §1006's rows stay where they are, written no more: «Echipa» reads both records and shows the newest acceptance of the version in force, and the legal list counts every acceptance of both as a reliance on its version.
- **The words.** `/admin/acord`: «Înainte să lucrezi în backoffice, citește angajamentul de mai jos și acceptă-l. Îl accepți la fiecare intrare în cont.» / “… You accept it each time you sign in.” — «în cont», not the brief's «în platformă»: the backoffice never says «platforma» / “the platform” (§522, the owner's own rule, which `plain-words.test.ts` holds); the legal text, which is not a screen, keeps «în platformă» beside its «platforma clubului». «Numele tău complet» typed each time and never prefilled, as §1006 has it; the tick never ticked for them. The guide in both languages: «Angajamentul echipei, la fiecare intrare» (not asked again in the same session; after «Ieși din cont» the next sign-in asks it again; for race day, sign in on your own phone the day before and stay signed in), «Conturi pentru voluntari și colegi», «Aprobă angajamentul echipei», and «Sarcini»' row — every step of the guide's two tasks about it within the backoffice's 200 characters, in both languages, held by the gate's test. `SETUP.md` §34 and §48, `AGENTS.md` §13.1.
- **The legal text.** Section 10 of the template said «la prima intrare în platformă după ce clubul l-a aprobat … O versiune nouă a angajamentului se acceptă din nou, la următoarea intrare»; it now says the undertaking is accepted at every sign-in while a version the club approved is in force, each acceptance recorded with the sign-in it answers, and a new version accepted again before working on. It is a draft the club approves on its own page, a lawyer first — an agent never approves a text, and nothing is seeded: a version approved before keeps «la prima intrare» until then, and `/admin/legal` and the daily «Șabloanele textelor legale s-au schimbat» name it.
- **Nothing else moves**: the gate's kinds (a page sent to `/admin/acord` with its way back, an action or a route refused `FORBIDDEN`), the layouts' bare shell, the one read per request, sign-out, the Administrators.

**Refused, and why.**

- Rewriting a pre-change session's token at the acceptance (Auth.js's `unstable_update`): an update runs the same `jwt` callback a browser can trigger by posting to `/api/auth/session`, so letting an update write the moment would let a browser choose it; the fallback asks such a session once and writes nothing to its token.
- A fixed date standing for the release: the deploy's moment is not known when the code is written, and an acceptance made under §1006 between that date and the deploy would answer.
- The token's `iat`: Auth.js signs the token again on every session read, so `iat` is the last refresh, not the sign-in.
- Dropping §1006's unique key to keep every acceptance in its table: a contraction beside an expansion (AGENTS.md §7.6), while the release before still writes `ON CONFLICT` on that key during the deploy. Copying §1006's rows into the new record: they answer no sign-in, and copied they would spare the pre-change sessions their one ask.
- Signing everybody out at the release, or a shorter session: nobody is signed out; the next sign-in is when it is asked.
- Prefilling «Numele tău complet» with the account's name: the name typed is the signature, as §1006 has it.
- Storing an acceptance's moment as the later of the press and the sign-in, so the moments alone always agree: the record would keep a moment no server read; the row's own sign-in answers it instead, and `accepted_at` stays what the press's server read.

**For the lawyer, not decided here.** Whether an acceptance at every sign-in is proportionate (art. 5(1)(c) GDPR), and how long each one is kept — they now accumulate, one per sign-in, and still go with the account (`docs/OWNER-TODO.md` item 26).
changelogLine: - **The team's undertaking at every sign-in** — a «Voluntar», «Redactor», «Organizator» or «Tehnic» accepts it each time they sign in, not once per account: the session carries the moment it was signed in, every acceptance is kept with the sign-in it answers, «Acord» and the guide say so, and the template's section 10 now does too — a draft for the club to approve. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Amends criterion 220. Given an approved version of `STAFF_DATA_AGREEMENT` in force, then a Voluntar, a Redactor, an Organizer or a Tehnic owes it once per sign-in, not once per account: the session carries the moment it was signed in — `signedInAt`, written by Auth.js's `jwt` callback when a sign-in hands it Zitadel's `account` and only then, kept as the token is refreshed and never written by an update a browser posts, and written beside the account's id by the development sign-in, both dropped at sign-out — and the gate owes the version in force unless the account accepted it at or after that moment or an acceptance names that very sign-in — one stored a little before the sign-in it names, its server's clock behind the sign-in's, answers it all the same, so no session is asked over and over until sign-out —, so the next sign-in is asked again while the same session, or one signed in before an acceptance made since on another device, is not; a session signed in before §NNN, which carries no moment, is asked once — until the account accepts at a sign-in — and not again until its next sign-in, no token rewritten and nobody signed out; an acceptance made once per account under §1006 answers no sign-in; the gate's kinds, the one read per request, sign-out and the Administrators are as criterion 220 has them (2026-11-20, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criterion 221. Given `/admin/acord`, then it says «Îl accepți la fiecare intrare în cont.» (“You accept it each time you sign in.”), «Numele tău complet» is empty and «Am citit și accept angajamentul» unticked at every sign-in, and every press that accepts is kept — one row per account, version and sign-in in `staff_team_agreement_sign_in_acceptances` (migration `0225`, expand only), with the declarations' proof and the sign-in it answers (`signed_in_at`, null for a session from before §NNN), audited with the version and that sign-in and never the name —, a second press for the same sign-in writing nothing; §1006's acceptances stay as they were; «Echipa» shows the newest acceptance of the version in force from either record, and the legal list counts every one as a reliance on its version (2026-11-20, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given the platform's template of `STAFF_DATA_AGREEMENT`, then its section 10 says, in Romanian and English, that the undertaking is accepted electronically at every sign-in while a version the club approved is in force, each acceptance recorded with the sign-in it answers, and a new version accepted again before working on — never «la prima intrare» or once —; a version approved before keeps its words until the club approves the regenerated draft, which no agent approves and no seed writes (2026-11-20, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: the team's undertaking at every sign-in, every acceptance kept with the sign-in it answers
